editorial.marketOverview: The three-day outlook remains Neutral — Downside Risk for November 12, 13 and 16. The Nvidia governance crisis continues to dominate Nasdaq futures, with reported premarket losses now spreading to other chipmakers. No Thursday regular-session price discovery has yet confirmed a broad index breakdown.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters reported Nasdaq-100 futures -0.79%, NVDA approximately -7% premarket and Intel, Marvell and Micron -2.6% to -3.4%. This offers stronger evidence of semiconductor premarket contagion than the earlier overnight futures reading but is consistent with the existing downside-risk scenario. Curated Open Watch rose to 158 events, adding Fractile's $720 million AI-chip funding at a reported $7 billion valuation; no attributable US market reaction was verified.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Positive November 11 Nasdaq and SOX cash closes predate the Nvidia governance headlines and cannot be combined as simultaneous confirmation with Thursday premarket weakness. The broader chip premarket selling is concerning but does not by itself establish a cash-session sector breakdown. November 10 2Y 4.731% and 10Y 4.988% give +25.7 basis points, correctly scaled but stale; synchronized yields, volatility, breadth and FedWatch remain unverified. Lower oil prices may temper inflation risk, but are asynchronous.
editorial.threeDayPath: Thursday November 12 tests whether the Nvidia-driven premarket selloff persists into regular trading, whether SOX underperforms QQQ, and whether jobless claims shift yields. Friday November 13's scheduled PPI can reinforce or reverse the rates narrative. Monday November 16 will test whether the sector stabilizes or broad Nasdaq weakness persists.
editorial.bullCase: Orderly official Nvidia leadership clarification, resilient AI infrastructure demand, semiconductor recovery versus QQQ, improving breadth and contained volatility/yields could restore a cautiously bullish bias. Foxconn's demand outlook and Fractile financing are fundamental support, not verified price confirmation.
editorial.bearCase: A confirmed disruptive Nvidia leadership change or continued NVDA/peer losses spilling into SOX and QQQ, with widening negative breadth, higher VXN and yields or hotter PPI, would support a bearish downgrade. Proposed export controls should not be treated as enacted.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor official Nvidia board announcements, the US cash open, time-aligned NVDA/SOX/QQQ, SMH/SOXX, VXN/VIX, Nasdaq breadth and Treasury 2Y/10Y. Verify jobless claims, Cisco and Applied Materials earnings timing and reactions, Friday PPI, and Monday follow-through. Distinguish new curated events from their unverified expected impact.
